## What this PR does

One or two sentences.

## Stack and file scope

- Stack: (dotnet, react, python, etc.)
- Files changed: (list them)

## Why

What problem does this solve, or what gap does it close? Link to an issue if there is one.

## Type of change

- [ ] New stack extension (claiming an open stack — full four-file submission)
- [ ] New pattern or anti-pattern in an existing stack
- [ ] Change to a standing order (requires strong justification)
- [ ] Documentation fix (typo, broken link, factual correction)
- [ ] Documentation improvement (clarification, better example)
- [ ] Tooling, repo hygiene, or CI change
- [ ] Other (describe)

## Real-world grounding

FSE extensions are based on shipped work, not theory. Briefly describe the project or situation that motivated this change. You don't have to share anything proprietary.

## Scope check

- [ ] This change stays within the stack folder it belongs to
- [ ] This change is consistent with the structure used by the dotnet reference folder
- [ ] This change does not contradict the core methodology in fse-core
- [ ] This change does not introduce marketing language or stack-rivalry tone

## If this is a new stack extension

- [ ] All four files (README, standing-orders, patterns, anti-patterns) are present
- [ ] Every standing order has a stated consequence or failure mode
- [ ] Every pattern is grounded in production work I have personally done
- [ ] I am committing to maintain this stack going forward
- [ ] I have read CONTRIBUTING.md

## Breaking change?

Does this change the meaning of an existing standing order, pattern, or anti-pattern? If yes, explain.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have read CONTRIBUTING.md
- [ ] I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
- [ ] I am submitting under Apache 2.0
- [ ] I am the author of this content, or I have the right to contribute it

## Anything else

Notes for reviewers, open questions, things you're unsure about.
